paper.title_en: Derivation of Hubble's Law and the Accelerated Expansion of the Universe from Hamiltonian Dynamics
paper.abstract_en: In classical works, the Hubble constant is defined in terms of a metric. In this paper, we argue that this is invalid for many reasons and define the Hubble constant in terms of matter, following the work by Milne and McCrea. It turns out that the Hubble law is a general law of Hamiltonian mechanics, and Milne and McCrea's theory of an expanding universe can be extended not only to the relativistic case, but also to a special class of isotropic Hamiltonians. This allows us to explain the accelerated expansion as a simple relativistic effect without using Einstein's lambda, dark energy, or new particles, more specifically, as an exact consequence of the classical Einstein action for particles moving along geodesics.
